family.name: pp_exchanger
family.title: Shell-and-tube exchanger: dimensionless temperature profiles over its design space
family.domain: energy / process and HVAC heat exchangers

reference.name: Kern + Gnielinski film coefficients with the 1-2 exchanger energy equations (epsilon-NTU)
reference.citation: Kern (1950) via pinneapple_physics.closed_form.heat_exchanger.kern_shell; Gnielinski (1976) and Incropera ch. 8 for the tube side; Nagle's 1-2 model integrated in pinneapple_physics.closed_form.heat_exchanger.one_two_exchanger_ode
assumptions: water on both sides with properties held at 45 degC (cp 4182, mu 6.5e-4, k 0.64, rho 990)
1-2 exchanger, shell fluid well mixed across each section, tube passes in counterflow
constant UA along the exchanger, no fouling, no heat loss to the surroundings
shell stream is C_min by construction, which is what the 1-2 model assumes

split.policy: random by geometry, fixed by the seed: a held-out body is never a training body

ensemble_spread.note: standard deviation between the bagged ensemble heads, not a confidence level

probes.name: a 300-tube shell, twice the trained tube count
reasons: operating parameters [2] outside the trained range

probes.name: a 9 m exchanger, 2.6x the trained length
reasons: geometry 2.28x farther from the training designs than usual
operating parameters [3, 4] outside the trained range

ood.threshold: the library's own: geometry-code distance over the 95th percentile of the training nearest-neighbour distances, above 1.5x
ood.note: reported as measured: a probe the model does not flag is not thereby inside its validity domain

measured_here: held-out relative L2 0.279 on 4 designs of 320 points, tolerance 0.02
constant-field baseline on the same designs: 0.6489
OOD: 2/2 probes outside the family flagged, 2/4 held-out designs flagged
not_measured: the reference itself: analytic — Kern + Gnielinski film coefficients with the 1-2 exchanger energy equations (epsilon-NTU), with the assumptions it lists
agreement with a solver or with measured data for any geometry of this family
whether the ensemble spread is calibrated: it is the spread between bootstrap heads
behaviour outside the declared geometry and operating bounds of the family
